issues.claim: §4.4 S5a Trace (2)'s one list of the pull's impassables (ARCHITECTURE l. 6602; P2) now ends 'every held building's strip and a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips, each widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): no line, band or wall strip across one)'. Every pull, cost field and reader of them cites that list: V06 §3.7.4 (2)'s cost field, *beneath* (l. 3076-3080) and a hand `contractWall`. 'A held building's strip' is already 'widened all round by the meeting wall's strips' width' by its definition (§2.7's laws' terms, l. 2642-2643), and law 1 (9) keeps the line alone out of it (l. 2736-2738). *Line and band* reads it so: 'each count the band's half already, so a line is kept out of them as they are drawn' (l. 3073-3074). Read naturally ('each'), the list widens it a second time; read with the definition, it does not. The pipeline seat's note says 'never twice' (assemble-r7w §8), but the design text does not. The doubled build keeps law 1, but it excludes every line between one and two wall-strip widths (about 15-30 m each) of the held span, which law 2 (a) admits ('only shapes law 1 admits', l. 2812-2813). So a hand `contractWall`, held to 'its own pull, within its own search band' of 40 m, 'its band never widened' (F-WALL, l. 9855), is refused `refuse.raised.meeting` where the single build bends it to a lawful crossing a span away. An epoch contraction or re-anchored stretch waits where the single build lays it. F-WALL's generation rung is unaffected, since it re-pulls with law 1's own exclusions (l. 9855). Refusing or waiting while a lawful local shape exists breaks J144's RULE ('where two such structures meet, their shapes change to make the meeting coherent') as the program's (G3) reads it ('where no local shape makes the meeting coherent', PROGRESS J144; Part P pass 8, PRB7H-GEN-04 (i); adjudication-r7w's regrade of VF7v-GEN-03). It can also fail T110-2 (4)'s held-building run ('the circuit crossing the deck line clear of that span's strip …', l. 19451-19455) and T-V4-80 (i) (V04 l. 3181). Not every outcome keeps the owner rules and the named tests, so this is no valid choice (J151): major.
issues.required_change: §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 6602): 'every held building's strip and a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips, each widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): no line, band or wall strip across one)' → 'every held building's strip, already so widened by its definition (law 1 (9)), and a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips, these widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): no line, band or wall strip across one)'.

issues.claim: No family bar runs six outcomes the fix passes wrote, so a build of the old text passes every bar. Three are the second pass's regraded majors, whose old outcomes Part P pass 8 ruled against J144 and J147 (1) as the program reads them. (a) §4.4 S5a Trace (2)'s pin trigger (l. 6603; P3): 'or nearer its foot than the first point beyond the foot', and a pin whose 'band or wall strips there would lie over a raised way's ends … moves along its arterial'. T110-2 (3) runs only a boundary that 'falls on an S4 viaduct's ramp' (l. 19363-19365). (b) §4.2 S3 (7)'s carried-way gate 'moved along the way within (9)'s search band …, and only where §2.7's laws give it no lawful gate so, the way re-routed' (l. 6227; P4). T110-2 (6)'s seeds give a lawful gate at the crossing or none in the band (l. 19558-19567), so a re-route-first build passes. (c) §4.4 S5a Outer moats' 'a carried way decked at its gate as at stage 1' (l. 6633-6638; P5). Every carried-way run is at stage 1 (l. 19560). (d) S3 (7)'s gate-route trigger 'nearer its foot than the first point beyond the foot' (round-7v pick). T110-2 (2) runs only a first point on the deck (l. 19332-19334). (e) F-WALL's hand clause, 'its band never widened' (l. 9855; D4, M7). No fixture puts the only lawful crossing beyond the band but within `wall.barrierReachM` (T110-2 (4), l. 19433). (f) A castle sited or resized by hand, 'moved whole to the nearest lawful site …, measured back along the drag' (§7.1 row, l. 11343; V09 §4.9). T110-2 (3)'s castles are sited only at generation and at a regeneration (l. 19375-19380). Each wrong build keeps law 1 and passes §5.3's row and T110-4, so under J146 and J151 this is minor.

issues.claim: This is a residue of the class ruling's C6, at T110-2 (6)'s New random runs (l. 19533-19540). They read 'its seed searched so that the new ring's boundary meets one of the aqueduct's supports where its channel runs above the ring's top — the trace crossing the deck line under a span, never at a support, …' and 'on (1)'s variant the crossing merged wherever the boundary meets the deck line where its channel runs within the ring's height'. The seed fixes the level only where the boundary (S3 (6)'s pick) meets the deck line. The trace is S3 (9)'s pull, whose crossing is its own cost's within a 40 m search band (law 2 (a); §4.4 S5a Trace (2)). There the channel may come within the ring's height, where a merged crossing at a support is lawful (law 1 (2)), or, on the merged variant, rise above it. C5 fixed the same pin at T110-2 (4) ('wherever the circuit's search band and the strokes' reach meet the aqueduct'). S0 makes the bar assert the laws' outcome (l. 19256-19263), so no correct build fails: minor.
issues.required_change: T110-2 (6) (l. 19533-19540): 'its seed searched so that the new ring's boundary meets one of the aqueduct's supports where its channel runs above the ring's top —' → 'its seed searched so that the new ring's boundary meets one of the aqueduct's supports and its channel runs above the ring's top wherever S3's pull's search band meets the aqueduct —'; and 'and on (1)'s variant the crossing merged wherever the boundary meets the deck line where its channel runs within the ring's height' → 'and on (1)'s variant, its channel within the ring's height wherever that search band meets the aqueduct, the crossing merged wherever the trace crosses the deck line'.

issues.claim: This is a twin of the class ruling's C2 and C10, at T-V4-63 (V04 l. 3164): 'on a CITY fixture whose viaduct holds a `vault` span with its arch vault, passed beneath by an epoch circuit and, on a second run, by a hand `drawWall` … — that arch vault removed … in the wall's commit, … the circuit's case run again with that `vault` span breached with its chamber first … and that vault removed in the circuit's commit'. An epoch circuit's crossing is its cost field's own (law 2 (a)), and nothing in the fixture puts its band or wall strips over that span's strip. C2 (T110-2 (4)) and C10 (T-V4-80 (i), 'its seed searched so that the circuit's line crosses the deck line under that span') fixed the same pin. The sweep read T-V4-63's other clauses as holding and missed this one. S0 governs: minor.
issues.required_change: V04 T-V4-63 (V04 l. 3164): 'passed beneath by an epoch circuit and, on a second run, by a hand `drawWall`' → 'passed beneath by an epoch circuit (its seed searched so that the circuit's line crosses the deck line under that span; §2.7's laws, law 2 (a)) and, on a second run, by a hand `drawWall`'.
